subject: Client embargo request: NebulaTech reference release
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@nebulatech.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: purchasing@nebulatech.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request to hold NebulaTech case study publication

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the draft case study and for working with our marketing team. After our internal post-incident review (attached summary), leadership has asked us to pause any public-facing case studies or testimonials that mention the June service disruption until after our renewal conversation in late August. This is a sensitivity request tied to an ongoing customer communications plan — it's not a denial of the story, just a request for a temporary embargo.

Can you please confirm you will hold publication and any press/promotional use of the draft until we clear it? If helpful, I've attached the internal incident summary and copied purchasing for contract context.

Appreciate your flexibility,
Elena Ruiz
VP of Product Marketing
NebulaTech

Attachment: nebula_incident_summary_2026-06.pdf (PDF, 230KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@nebulatech.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to hold NebulaTech case study publication

Team — forwarding the request from NebulaTech. Key asks: hold publication and any social/press mentions until they give the green light (they've tied this to renewal timing).

Questions:
- Legal: do we have any obligation per the testimonial release or our contract that forces publication? (see deal NB-2025-44)
- CS (Marcus): how material is this incident to the customer relationship? Is there a churn risk if we push?
- Marketing (Laura): can we prepare a redacted short quote or a neutral blurb that we could use in product pages if needed, or do we have to fully pull the content?

I recommended we acknowledge and confirm the embargo in writing while we triage internal options. Laura, Marcus — can you advise with a one-paragraph recommendation by EOD tomorrow? I can loop legal if needed.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Customer Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request to hold NebulaTech case study publication

Olga — quick context from CS: the June incident caused a multi-hour outage for NebulaTech's non-critical batch reporting pipeline. They escalated (covered in the attached postmortem) but we resolved and implemented the fixes. Renewal is currently in late August and there have been some hard questions from their execs about continuity and auditability.

Recommendation: honor the embargo for now. Two reasons — 1) publishing before their execs are comfortable introduces unnecessary friction in renewal, and 2) they explicitly requested it, so publishing risks damaging trust. That said, if Marketing needs a quote for demand gen, propose a one-line neutral blurb (e.g., “NebulaTech leverages Redwood Inference for production inference workloads”) that contains no mention of the outage and is pre-approved by their comms team.

I'm attaching our renewal timeline and the internal incident summary we've received. If Legal confirms no contractual obligation to publish, I'd keep the full case study in draft until after the renewal or until they lift the embargo.

Attachments: renewal-timeline-NEB-2026.xlsx, nebula_incident_summary_2026-06.pdf

—Marcus
Customer Success Director
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context. I agree with Marcus — we should respect the request and mark the draft as embargoed. Practical plan:

1) Publish hold: I'll move the draft-case-study-redwood-nebulatech-v1.docx into an "Embargoed - Do Not Publish" folder and restrict distribution to marketing+legal.
2) Short neutral blurb: prepare one-line approved language for product pages that says "NebulaTech uses Redwood Inference for production inference workloads." We'll send that to Elena for express written approval; no mention of the outage.
3) Redacted case study option: prepare a heavily redacted one-pager (no dates, no incident details, no metrics) that we can use if sales needs a quick reference; again, only if Elena explicitly approves.
4) Legal check: Priyom — please confirm there are no terms in NB-2025-44 or the testimonial release that obligate us to publish or that prevent an embargo. If Legal flags any issue we'll escalate but I don't expect it.

I will confirm once the draft is moved and will prepare the blurb for Elena to sign off on. If everyone is aligned I'll reply to Elena to confirm we will hold publication and propose the short neutral blurb.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Marketing
Redwood Inference
